title: The danger behind the perfect shark picture
standfirst: Some travellers are getting dangerously close to wild sharks for dramatic social-media footage. Scientists say the risk affects both people and the animals.

source.name: BBC News
source.originalTitle: The influencers getting bitten while chasing the perfect shark shot

paragraphs: In April, Brazilian lawyer and social-media personality Tayane Dalazen joined a shark-diving trip off the coast of Brazil. She noticed that many sharks were swimming near the surface. Later, she learnt that the tour organisers had been feeding them so that they would come closer to the tourists.

During the dive, a nurse shark more than two metres long bit Dalazen on the thigh and held her underwater for several seconds. Although the pain was intense, she stayed calm because she knew that fighting the animal could make the situation worse. The shark eventually released her, and she escaped with deep cuts. Video of the incident was later watched tens of millions of times. Dalazen says she did not touch or provoke the shark, but she accepts that she was too close.

Shark bites remain extremely rare. Worldwide, the yearly number of unprovoked bites has stayed at roughly 70 for about three decades. However, researchers have noticed a rise in incidents involving people who are trying to film sharks. At least three social-media influencers have been bitten in less than a year. One study of wildlife-swimming trips found that influencers and photographers were the visitors most likely to ignore safety advice.

Scientists say getting too close can harm sharks as well as humans. A shark may bite defensively when a person enters its space. Approaching or touching it can also increase its stress hormones, which may weaken its immune system and affect its ability to reproduce. Some content creators argue that close-up videos educate the public and encourage shark conservation. They also say viewers must take responsibility for their own choices.

Several shark experts disagree. They say that touching or riding a wild shark is harassment, not conservation, and does not produce the scientific evidence needed to protect shark populations. Meanwhile, shark tourism is becoming more popular; one travel website lists more than 140 shark experiences in the Maldives alone, and some promise visitors an unforgettable selfie. The experts’ message is simple: a dramatic picture may earn attention online, but getting it could have serious consequences.

easy.label: Start here
easy.prompt: In your own words, what happens in the text?

easy.label: Find the facts
easy.prompt: Where was Tayane Dalazen, and what kind of trip did she join?
easy.support: Try: “She was off the coast of Brazil, and she joined…”

easy.label: Before the bite
easy.prompt: What had the tour organisers been doing, and why had they done it?
easy.support: Try using “had been feeding” and “so that”.

easy.label: During the bite
easy.prompt: What did the nurse shark do, and how did Tayane react?

easy.label: Afterwards
easy.prompt: How did the incident end, and what injuries did Tayane have?
easy.support: Answer in two complete past-tense sentences.

easy.label: Understand a number
easy.prompt: About how many unprovoked shark bites happen each year, and for how long has that number stayed similar?
easy.support: Try using “has stayed” in your answer.

easy.label: Spot the change
easy.prompt: What rise have researchers noticed in recent years?

easy.label: Cause and effect
easy.prompt: How can getting too close to a shark harm the animal?
easy.support: Give at least two effects mentioned in the text.

easy.label: Two viewpoints
easy.prompt: What do some content creators say their close-up videos achieve?

easy.label: Final message
easy.prompt: What warning do the shark experts give at the end of the text?
easy.support: Explain the warning without copying the final sentence.

challenge.label: Explain a cause
challenge.prompt: How might the organisers’ earlier decision to feed the sharks have changed the danger during Tayane’s dive?
challenge.support: Explain what they had done first, then what happened later.

challenge.label: Imagine differently
challenge.prompt: If Tayane had panicked and fought the shark, what might have happened?
challenge.support: Try: “If she had…, the shark might have…”

challenge.label: Interpret evidence
challenge.prompt: Shark bites are very rare, yet filming-related incidents are rising. How can both statements be true?

challenge.label: Judge an argument
challenge.prompt: Content creators say close-up videos support conservation, while scientists say they can be harassment. Which argument is stronger, and why?
challenge.support: Give your judgement and support it with evidence from the text.

challenge.label: Responsibility
challenge.prompt: Who is most responsible for risky wildlife content: tourists, tour companies, social-media platforms or viewers?
challenge.support: Use “should”, “must” or “ought to” to explain your choice.

challenge.label: Make a rule
challenge.prompt: What rules should shark-tour companies follow, and what should happen if a visitor ignores them?
challenge.support: Try: “Companies should… If a visitor…, then…”

challenge.label: Connect experience
challenge.prompt: Think of another situation in which someone took a risk for a photograph or video. What happened, and what lesson does it give us now?
challenge.support: Tell the past event first, then explain the present lesson.

challenge.label: Change perspective
challenge.prompt: Imagine you manage the tour company. What would you say the company did wrong, and what safety policy do you have now?
challenge.support: Move clearly from the past mistake to the present policy.

challenge.label: Look ahead
challenge.prompt: If shark tourism keeps growing in the same way, what will or might happen to tourists and sharks in the future?
challenge.support: Use both “will” and “might” if you can.

challenge.label: Bring it together
challenge.prompt: Using the incident as evidence, explain what people have learnt, what they should do now and what could change in the future.
challenge.support: Give one past point, one present recommendation and one future prediction.
